title: Stylebook for Android? The Best Alternatives (2026)
h1: Is Stylebook on Android? No, but these apps come close
excerpt: Stylebook for Android doesn't exist: the app is iPhone and iPad only. See the best Android alternatives, a comparison table and how to switch over.
tldr: No. Stylebook is only on iPhone and iPad, and its official FAQ says an Android version isn't planned 'at the moment'. On Android, Indyx is the closest match for manual planning and cost per wear, Whering is the biggest free option, and Fits suits people who liked Stylebook's outfit canvas.
body:
No. There is no Stylebook app for Android: Stylebook runs only on iPhone and iPad, and its official FAQ answers the Android question with "Not at the moment. As of 2025, we are focusing on iOS." So Stylebook for Android isn't something you can download, from Google Play or anywhere else.

The closest Android alternatives are Indyx (free, with manual outfit planning and cost per wear), Whering (free, with outfit shuffling and a web version) and Fits (free, with a canvas outfit builder). GetWardrobe is worth a look if you use a mix of Android and Apple devices. The details below come from each app's official site and its US Google Play and App Store listings, checked on 17 October 2026. We haven't tested the apps ourselves, and features change, so check the listing before you pay.

Why there's no Stylebook for Android

Stylebook is made by left brain / right brain, LLC and has only ever been an iOS app. The FAQ says it "is only available for iOS devices, including iPhone and iPad", there's no Google Play listing, and it doesn't run on desktop or laptop computers either. A few practical points follow from that:

  • Any "Stylebook APK" is unofficial. With no Android version, an APK on a download site can't have come from the developer. Sideloading one risks malware, and it won't be the real app.
  • A Chromebook won't help. Many Chromebooks run Android apps from Google Play, but Stylebook isn't on Google Play.
  • An iPad will. If you have an Android phone and an iPad, Stylebook runs on the iPad. You lose the convenience of checking your closet on your phone, but you keep the app.
  • Updates have slowed. The latest App Store version is 10.1, from 15 June 2025, and it needs iOS or iPadOS 17 or later. Worth knowing before you buy an iPad just for it.

What to look for in a Stylebook alternative

People who like Stylebook tend to stay for a specific set of features. Before you pick a replacement, decide which of these you'd miss:

  • A free-form canvas for arranging outfits yourself, with Outfit Shuffle for random mixes
  • A calendar to plan outfits or log what you wore
  • Cost per wear, closet value and lists of your most and least worn pieces
  • Visual packing lists
  • A one-time price instead of a subscription
  • No account: your closet stays on your device, and in iCloud if you turn sync on

The last two are the hardest to match on Android. The alternatives below are free to start and charge for extras, most of them keep your closet in an online account, and none of the listings checked here advertises an offline mode. If privacy decides it for you, read each app's data safety section on Google Play before signing up, and see our guide to the privacy downsides of wardrobe apps.

The best Stylebook alternatives on Android

Indyx: closest for people who plan by hand

If you liked Stylebook because you build outfits yourself and like seeing what you actually wear, Indyx is the nearest thing on Android. The free tier includes unlimited items, outfits, calendar entries and packing lists. You arrange outfits on drag-and-drop boards, cost per wear is calculated automatically, and you can sort your closet by wears. Backgrounds are removed from your photos, AI tags each item's category, subcategory and colour, and you can add pieces by forwarding a receipt or pasting a product link.

Indyx doesn't generate outfits. Its listing says "No random outfits styled by robots" and offers human stylists instead, starting at $60 for a virtual session on its site. The optional Insider membership, listed at $12.99 a month or $74.99 a year on the US App Store in October 2026, adds more analytics. The trade-offs: an online closet rather than on-device storage, and no web app. On Google Play it has 4.5 stars from 1.3K reviews and was updated on 13 October 2026.

Whering: the biggest free option

Whering is free on Android and iPhone, and it also has a web version and a Chrome extension, which makes cataloguing from a laptop easier. You can photograph pieces (it removes the background) or add them from a database of more than 100 million items. Dress Me shuffles your clothes into outfits, much like Stylebook's Outfit Shuffle. There's an outfit planner for events, packing lists with reminders, and stats including cost per wear, wear rate and your colour palette.

The Outfit Maker needs a paid Style Pass, and credit packs are sold in the app. Whering is far more social than Stylebook, with friends' closets and style submissions. On privacy, its Google Play data safety section says photos and videos may be shared with third parties. Google Play: 4.4 stars from 27.8K reviews and 5 million-plus downloads. For a closer look at how it stacks up against Stylebook and Indyx, see our Whering vs Indyx vs Stylebook comparison.

Fits: for fans of Stylebook's outfit canvas

Fits, from the German developer L. & J. Henne UG, is free with unlimited items and background removal. Its outfit tools are the most Stylebook-like here: a swipe outfit builder plus a free canvas, outfit mood boards and custom tags. There's a calendar for planning ahead or logging what you wore, and help with packing for a trip. Fits Pro adds unlimited AI outfit suggestions and AI detection of category, colour and season, and a September 2026 App Store update added an AI stylist chat that can suggest products.

Fits syncs between Android and Apple devices but has no web app, and cost per wear isn't listed. Don't confuse it with "Fits AI", a separate iPhone app. Google Play: 4.7 stars from 14.5K reviews.

GetWardrobe: if you switch between Android and Apple

GetWardrobe syncs across Android, iPhone, iPad, Mac and the web, so it suits anyone moving from iPhone to Android in stages, or keeping an iPad alongside an Android phone. The free tier covers up to 100 items (clothes and outfits together), with AI background removal and a starter version of its AI outfit generator. Premium is listed on its site at $49.99 a year in October 2026 (US dollars; it says prices may vary by region). It has an outfit calendar with local weather, cost per wear, most and least worn stats, capsules and, on Premium, packing lists. Google Play: 4.0 stars from 5K reviews.

Acloset: if you want an outfit suggested every morning

Acloset is AI-led. It suggests a daily outfit based on the weather and your schedule, and has an AI stylist chat, colour and fit analysis and weather-based trip packing. It still covers Stylebook basics such as an outfit calendar, wear tracking and cost per wear. It's free for up to 100 items, with ads, and subscriptions raise the limit. On Google Play it carries an Editors' Choice badge in the US, with 4.4 stars from 30.9K reviews.

Alta: free and on the web

Alta is free, and the App Store lists no in-app purchases. It suggests daily outfits from the weather and your schedule, builds outfits around a piece you choose, and has avatar try-on, a style calendar, cost per wear and packing lists. It runs on Android, iPhone and in a web browser. The catch is shopping: it has wishlists with price-drop alerts and suggests pieces to fill gaps in your closet, and its App Store label lists precise location and photos among the data linked to you.

Google Photos Wardrobe: automatic, but only in three countries

Google Photos can now build a wardrobe from clothes in photos of you, let you mix up to six items into an outfit and preview it on yourself with "Try it on". The catch is availability. Google's help page limits it to Brazil, India and the US, needs Android 10 or later and Face Groups turned on, and says it's rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers "as well as other select users"; non-subscribers need more than 1,000 photos of themselves. It scans photos from the past four years, and saved outfits count toward your storage. Google's pages don't describe wear tracking, cost per wear or packing lists, so it's closer to a moodboard of what you own than a Stylebook replacement.

FitWardrobe: ours, and not out yet

FitWardrobe is our app, and it isn't available yet. It's coming to Android and the web and will be free during early access. It works differently from Stylebook: you photograph a piece and AI tags its type, colour, pattern, season and formality, which you can correct, then you pick an occasion and get a complete outfit built only from clothes you own, with a one-line reason and one or two alternatives. The wardrobe is stored on your device, but tagging sends a compressed photo to Google's Gemini API and suggestions send item details to Groq, so the AI features need an internet connection (see our AI transparency page). It has no calendar, cost per wear or packing lists, the Stylebook features many people rely on. You can join the early-access list to hear when it opens.

Other names in search results

Smart Closet by Rabbit Tech has a feature list close to Stylebook's, including a calendar, travel packing, price per wear and backup and restore. But its Google Play listing hasn't been updated since 1 December 2025 and shows 2.2 stars. Pureple on Android lets you add items and build outfits for free, but its AI suggestions and calendar planning need Pureple Pro, and it's rated 2.5 stars on Google Play. Cladwell has rebranded as an AI stylist app, with a subscription for its main AI features, rather than a catalogue-and-stats tool. For a wider list, see our guide to the best digital wardrobe apps.

How to move from Stylebook to Android

Stylebook's FAQ and features page describe iCloud backup and syncing between Apple devices, but not an export that another app can read. Plan to re-add your clothes rather than transfer them. These steps keep the work down:

  1. Keep Stylebook until the new app is set up. Don't wipe your iPhone first. If you also have an iPad, sync Stylebook to it so a copy stays within reach.
  2. Screenshot the numbers you care about. Wear counts, cost per wear and Style Stats won't carry over, so capture what you'd miss.
  3. Send yourself your best looks. Stylebook can share looks by email or text message. Email the outfits you rely on to yourself so you can rebuild them.
  4. Find your original photos. If you added clothes from your camera roll, the originals are probably still in your iPhone's photo library. Back them up to Google Photos and they'll be there when you sign in on Android, or copy them to a computer.
  5. Use the shortcuts. Whering lets you add pieces from its item database, Indyx takes forwarded receipts and product links, and Fits can clip items from the web. Each saves photographing things you bought online.
  6. Start with what you wear most. Add the 20 or 30 pieces you reach for every week, say your everyday jeans, a navy jumper, two shirts and your usual trainers, use the app for a fortnight, then add the rest. Our guide to digitising your wardrobe covers photographing clothes quickly.

faq.q: Is there a Stylebook APK for Android?
faq.a: No official one. Stylebook's developer doesn't make an Android version, and its FAQ says the app is only available for iPhone and iPad. Any file labelled 'Stylebook APK' on a download site didn't come from the developer and could contain malware. On Android, install an alternative from Google Play instead, such as Indyx, Whering or Fits.

faq.q: What is the closest app to Stylebook on Android?
faq.a: For manual outfit planning and wear stats, Indyx is the closest: free unlimited items, drag-and-drop outfit boards, a calendar, packing lists and automatic cost per wear. If Stylebook's free-form outfit canvas is what you'd miss most, Fits is a better match. Neither copies Stylebook's no-account, on-device storage, since both keep your closet online.

Yes, in two places. Instant Import uses AI to remove the background from clothing photos, and on devices with Apple Intelligence it can generate clothing images from a description. It doesn't list AI outfit suggestions: you build outfits yourself on a canvas or use Outfit Shuffle for random combinations. On Android, Acloset and Alta are examples of apps that suggest outfits with AI.

faq.q: How much does Stylebook cost in 2026?
faq.a: Stylebook's FAQ lists it as a one-time charge of $4.99 in the US, not a subscription, and the US App Store shows no in-app purchases. Prices differ by country, so check your local App Store. It's sold only for iPhone and iPad, so you can't buy it on Google Play or use it on an Android phone.

faq.q: Is there a free Stylebook alternative for Android?
faq.a: Yes, several. Indyx's free tier includes unlimited items, outfits, calendar entries and packing lists. Fits is free with unlimited items and background removal. Whering is free with optional paid extras, and Alta is free with no in-app purchases listed. Acloset and GetWardrobe are free for up to 100 items. Limits change, so check each listing.

faq.q: Can I use Stylebook on a computer or Chromebook?
faq.a: No. Stylebook's FAQ says it doesn't run on desktop or laptop computers, and because there's no Google Play version, Chromebooks can't install it either. If you'd like to manage your wardrobe from a computer, Whering, GetWardrobe and Alta all have web versions you can open in a browser.
